newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds close up on central bank tender.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds close up on central bank tender.

text.p: Israeli bond prices closed up on Monday following a Bank of Israel intervention in the market to repurchase government bonds.

The index of government bonds was up 0.1 percent, of which bonds linked to the consumer price index were up 0.1 percent, those linked to the dollar were unchanged and the Gilon bond, unlinked, was up 0.1 percent.
"The bond market is calmer, but only on the surface. The crisis is not behind us. Long-term structural changes are needed," said Gad Hacker of Batucha Securities.
The Bank of Israel repurchased government bonds worth 250 million shekels but received supply totalling 1.254 billion shekels.
The central bank said only 354 million shekels of the offers were at market price, at which price the bank was buying.
"All in all bonds were up because of the security net. The market is calmer but it is not a change in direction," said Gidi Halpern of Meitav Investments and Securities.
Traders said that the offers to sell bonds above the market rate were made by provident funds who didn't really want to sell bonds but wanted to call attention to their plight.
Provident funds, long-term savings funds with special tax benefits, have been dumping bonds and selling stocks to meet massive public redemptions.
The central bank interventions are meant to stop falling bond prices and rising yields and to provide provident funds with the liquidity to meet the redemptions.

The Bank of Israel announced recently that it would intervene in the bond market to repurchase government bonds for the value of 750 million shekels. The intervention would be done through three tenders, the bank said, of which the first was held last week. The third tender for 250 million shekels will be held on Thursday.
Last month the central bank intervened in the bond market with two tenders for the total worth of 500 million shekels.
